Subject: Connectivity options for private deployment — quick primer and next steps

Hi Samira,

Thanks again for the time earlier. As discussed, I wanted to follow up with a short primer on the three common connectivity patterns customers use when deploying Redwood Private into a VPC/on-prem environment: VPC Peering, AWS PrivateLink (Interface Endpoints), and Site-to-Site (S2S) VPN. Attached is a two-page summary (rww-connectivity-options-v1.pdf) and a spreadsheet of the IP ranges you shared.

High-level differences (short):
- VPC Peering: simple L3 peering, low-latency, preserves source IPs, but is non-transitive and requires non-overlapping IP ranges across accounts/VPCs.
- PrivateLink (Interface Endpoint): exposes our API as endpoint network interfaces in your VPC — strong isolation, works across accounts without peering, source requests appear as from endpoint ENIs, good for controlled access and audit.
- Site-to-Site VPN: secure IPsec tunnel to on-prem — works for broader network access, policy-based routing needed, possible higher latency and bandwidth limits depending on your appliance.

Initial ask from our side:
1) Confirm whether you can share a definitive set of VPC CIDR(s) and any on-prem ranges you expect Redwood to reach. We got the preliminary sheet but want final ranges.
2) Any constraints on BGP or managed Transit Gateway usage?
3) Compliance question: do you require customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for endpoints or is platform-managed acceptable?

I'd propose this recommended path for GreenWave: start with PrivateLink to expose the Redwood API surface for production traffic (gives you per-endpoint control and easier least-privilege policies), and establish a Site-to-Site VPN for admin/ops traffic (backups, metrics export, lut). VPC peering is an OK option if you need IP-preservation and both sides control CIDRs and you want lowest latency, but it becomes painful if you plan multi-account expansion.

Can we set a 30-min technical review next week with your infra team and our solutions engineer (Dev Patel)? I can send a calendar invite.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Jonas / Lauren,

Thanks — I reviewed Samira's notes. Below is a concise technical assessment and recommended configuration with reasoning and follow-ups we should cover on the call.

Quick tradeoffs and answers to Samira's questions:
- Client IPs (PrivateLink): by default, traffic to our Service over PrivateLink comes from the endpoint ENI; the source IP seen by our backend is the ENI's address. To preserve original client IPs for logging/rate-limiting you can either:
  * Send a trusted X-Forwarded-For header from the endpoint (we support this if you control the client) OR
  * Use VPC Peering where the TCP connection originates from the client IP (no header required).
  Note: For strict audit requirements, we can add mutual TLS and embedded client cert CNs to map callers to identities.

- Throughput: PrivateLink performance is typically very good for API traffic; AWS has soft limits per ENI and per-VPC, but we can request increases. For sustained 350 Mbps bursts, a properly sized PrivateLink with multiple endpoints or using NLB+Proxy on our side suffices. S2S VPN throughput depends on your appliance (if using AWS managed VPN/Transit Gateway attachments, you can get >1 Gbps with tunnel aggregation; older appliances may be a bottleneck). VPC peering has no extra data path cost for intra-region peering and preserves low latency.

- BGP & S2S: We can peer via BGP; Redwood will accept a standard private ASN and support active/active tunnels. We will need:
  * your ASN and the public IPs for your VPN endpoints
  * BGP community and prefixes you plan to advertise
  * a failover plan (we prefer BFD for faster detection when available)

Recommended approach for GreenWave (minimizes friction + satisfies audit):
1) Primary production API traffic -> PrivateLink (Interface Endpoint). Rationale: easier cross-account access, endpoint-level IAM, and less blast radius during multi-account expansion. Pair this with mTLS for PHI endpoints.
2) Management / Ops plane -> S2S VPN (BGP) to your on-prem network for metrics export, admin tools, and internal backups. Configure VPN with active/active and advertise only ops prefixes to avoid routing overlap.
3) Reserve VPC Peering for low-level network scenarios where source IP preservation is mandatory and you control CIDRs end-to-end. If GreenWave remediates overlapping ranges, peering becomes an option but not recommended initially.

Open items for the call:
- Confirm exact CIDR list (Samira will provide).
- Confirm KMS/HSM approach for at-rest keys (we support either, but require the integration window).
- Decide on how to surface client IPs in PrivateLink flows (header vs sidecar proxy vs peering).

I'll draft a short network diagram for the meeting.

-Dev
